10.0.s.en: (1) The two silver trumpets and their use

10.0.0.en: In continuation of God's care for His people and His concern for the organization of their affairs, the Lord commanded Moses to make two trumpets of silver, and they were to be made by hammering and carving and not by casting, "of a whole piece." God made clear the first and basic purpose of making these two trumpets, which is communicating with the people and calling them and summoning them to journey or for other matters, as we shall see in the coming verses. It is also noted that the trumpets were spoken of earlier in (Lev 23). God commanded Moses to make two trumpets because there were only two priests, Eleazar and Ithamar the sons of Aaron. But later the number of priests increased greatly, so there were many trumpets: in the days of David there were seven trumpets (1 Chr 15:24) and in the days of Solomon there were a hundred and twenty trumpets (2 Chr 5:12).

10.1.0.en: If the priests blew both trumpets together, this was a sign summoning all the congregation of Israel to assemble before the door of the Tent for the announcement of something important.

10.2.0.en: But if they blew with one trumpet, this was a summons to the heads of thousands only, who are of course the chiefs supervising the heads of hundreds, the heads of fifties and the heads of tens, who were appointed to settle the people's problems as judges for them.

10.3.0.en: If the blowing of the trumpet was for the purpose of journeying, then at the first sound this was the signal for the three tribes of the east side to begin journeying, which are the tribes of Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

10.4.0.en: The second sound was for the departure of the camps encamped south of the Tent, which are the camps of the tribes of Reuben, Simeon and Gad. Although the third and fourth sounds for the departure of the rest of the camps are not mentioned afterward, it is implicitly understood and the order of the journeying is known: the camps of the west were the third, then the camps of the north.

10.5.0.en: You shall blow (strike): that is, blowing the two trumpets with an ordinary, broken blast.

10.5.1.en: You shall shout: that is, blowing with a continuous, loud blast.

10.5.2.en: God distinguished between two ways of using the trumpets, each way used in a specific manner for a specific purpose. At the time of journeying the sound of the two trumpets is continuous, unbroken and very loud, so that everyone is alerted to the event of departure, and this method was called shouting. But if the sound was ordinary and broken, it was understood from it that it was to summon the congregation without their journeying, and this method was called blowing (striking) the trumpets.

10.6.0.en: The blowing was limited to the priests, who are the sons of Aaron and their offspring only, but at the feasts, such as the Feast of Shouting, the Levites proclaimed the feast by shouting with the trumpets among the people (Lev 23:23).

10.7.0.en: In your land: that is, the land of Canaan.

10.7.1.en: That oppresseth you: that attacks you.

10.7.2.en: God also commanded the use of the trumpets in a state of war. If circumstances compelled the people to war and to defend their promised land against their enemies, they were also to use the trumpets, and the purpose of this, besides alerting the soldiers and the people to war, was that it be a sign of prayer and of taking refuge in God, as shown by His saying "and ye shall be remembered before the Lord," meaning that when the Lord sees the people's recourse to Him He gives them victory over their enemies. And indeed the trumpets were used afterward in all the wars of the people, as happened with the walls of Jericho in the days of Joshua, and likewise the war with the Midianites in the days of Gideon (Judg 7:19).

10.8.0.en: The beginnings of your months: the start of the months.

10.8.1.en: The last of the matters in which the Lord asked Moses and the people to use the trumpets is the joyful announcement of the feasts and of the beginnings of the months of the religious year, which were also celebrated, and the trumpets were also blown at the offering of the sacrifices of the feasts and of the spiritual occasions.

10.8.2.en: They shall be to you for a memorial before your God: that is, these feasts and celebrations bear witness for you that you have kept the commandments of the Lord and done as He commanded, so that His heart is pleased with you and He blesses your feasts and your spiritual seasons.

10.8.3.en: The sound of the trumpets signifies the word of God that the Church teaches her people.

10.8.4.en: The trumpets have disappeared and have no use in Christianity any more, but in their place have come what is stronger than they, the prayers of the Church's Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), which the heart shouts before the mouth ... Have you ever taken part in the Church's Tasbeha prayers ... and have you meditated on the power of their spiritual meanings and the peace of heart they give to whoever repeats them and shouts them ... Do not let this matter pass you by, and try to begin with the simple, especially since they have become available on tapes and in the Arabic language as well.

10.9.s.en: (2) The departure from the wilderness of Sinai

10.9.0.en: After eleven months and nineteen days that the people spent in the wilderness of Sinai, for their coming down to the wilderness was at the beginning of the third month of the first year (Ex 19:1) and their departure from it on the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud, that is, the pillar of cloud, was taken up from over the Tent, as a clear sign from God for the beginning of the people's movement.

10.9.1.en: As a summary of the events of this period we can say that the most important of its events were:

10.9.2.en: 1- Seeing the glory of God when Moses and the chiefs went up to the mountain.

10.9.4.en: 3- The numbering of the people, the firstborn and the Levites.

10.9.5.en: 4- The setting up of the tent of meeting.

10.9.6.en: 5- Receiving the rite of the sacrifices and the feasts.

10.9.7.en: 6- The ordination of the priests and the setting up and consecration of the Levites for the service.

10.10.0.en: The children of Israel left the wilderness of Sinai heading north, and after a journey of three days they reached the wide wilderness of Paran, in which they afterward spent 38 years. The wilderness of Paran is a wide wilderness that includes the middle of present-day Sinai and extends to the west of the city of El-Arish in the north, and passes beyond the Gulf of Aqaba, and merges with the wilderness of Zin ... See the map at the end of the book.

10.11.0.en: They first took their journey: that is, they journeyed for the first time.

10.11.1.en: The first journey of the people began as the Lord commanded Moses and made clear to him the order of this journey in the second chapter (ch. 2:9 ...). The inspired text has shown us here the people's commitment and obedience to the order that God set, and has given us the detail of this journey in the following verses (vv. 14-28).

10.12.0.en: In the first place went the standard of the camp: a figure for the journeying of the company bearing its standard (its flag). Host – hosts: that is, the strong men counted for war.

10.12.2.en: According to their hosts: according to the order of their company.

10.12.3.en: God already announced the order of this journey (ch. 2), so we shall summarize this journey here.

10.12.4.en: 1- The journeying of the first group, which is the group of Judah and includes the three eastern tribes. The names of the tribes are mentioned, "Judah, Issachar and Zebulun," as are the names of the chiefs of these tribes.

10.12.5.en: 2- The second group was of the clans of the Levites, the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the outer Tent without its inner contents and followed directly after the group of Judah.

10.12.6.en: 3- The third group: this was of the southern tribes and included the camp or tribe of Reuben, then Simeon and Gad under the standard of Reuben.

10.12.7.en: 4- The fourth group: this was of the third division of the divisions of the Levites, which is the division of the Kohathites, who carried on their shoulders, without wagons, the contents, furnishings and implements of the inner tabernacle such as the ark, the table of the showbread and the lampstand.

10.12.8.en: 5- The fifth group: this is the camp of Ephraim, and it included the tribes "Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin," which were situated on the west side of the tent of meeting.

10.12.9.en: 6- The last group: this is the group of the sons of Dan, and its three tribes are "Dan, Asher and Naphtali," which are the northern tribes, and this group was the rear of all the people.

10.12.10.en: Note: observe God's wisdom in the journeying of the Levites, in that He made them journey in two stages. The first stage (v. 17) is the journeying of the Gershonites and the Merarites, who carried the tabernacle and the heavy things (using the wagons), after the journeying of the tribes of Judah, and after their journeying comes the group of the tribes of Reuben before the group of the Kohathites who carried the light contents of the sanctuary (v. 21). This was so that God might give a span of time to the first group of the Levites to take down the Tent and set it up, so that when the others came they put its contents inside it.

10.13.0.en: Hobab: he is the son of Reuel, that is, the brother of Zipporah the wife of Moses, and Reuel is the father-in-law of Moses; and likewise in the custom of the Arabs Hobab, the brother of Zipporah the wife of Moses, is also regarded as the father-in-law of Moses. The name Hobab means beloved.

10.13.1.en: Moses asked Hobab to accompany them on their journey in the wilderness so that he might receive the good things of God that He had promised them, since they were going to move from the wilderness of Sinai to the wilderness of Paran on their way to the Promised Land.

10.14.0.en: Hobab's reply was an excuse because of the difficulty of leaving his land and his kindred, as is the case with many people who do not leave their homes for the unknown.

10.15.0.en: Moses repeated his request, making clear this time his need for Hobab as a helper who knew the desert and the wilderness better than anyone, so that he would be to the people like the eye that sees and guides a man to his way. Hobab of course knew the terrain of the region better than anyone, that is, he knew the pastures and the springs of water, so he would be a guide for them in the wilderness.

10.15.1.en: This does not cancel Moses' faith that God is the true leader of His people by means of the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, but he encourages Hobab that he has a work and a service with them, which is guiding them to some springs of water on their way, although the basis is the water that flows from the rock and that the Lord God gives them.

10.16.0.en: A repetition of the same offer that Moses made to Hobab in (v. 29), to share in the good things that God promised the people. No answer from Hobab is mentioned here, nor whether he went with them or not, although there is a reference to the going of the family of Moses' wife to the Promised Land in (Judg 4:11), and therefore it is most likely that he went with Moses.

10.16.1.en: Some saw in Moses a loving heart that does not forget a kindness, and, as the heart of a zealous servant, he wished to repay the favor to his wife's family by their sharing with him in the journey and then in the good things that God would give His people, and as a zealous servant he pressed his request more than once ...; do we too have this heart that calls and preaches to distant souls to share in the good things of Christ and the Church!!?

10.17.s.en: (4) The ark goes before the journey

10.17.0.en: The mount of the Lord: that is, Mount Horeb in the wilderness of Sinai.

10.17.1.en: To search out a resting place for them: an expression meaning that God would guide them where to encamp.

10.17.2.en: Was the ark going before the people?...! According to the order that God set, the ark was carried by the Kohathites, who are the fourth group of the journeying groups, and consequently the ark would be in the middle, and this agrees with providing the greatest protection for the ark in case they met enemies on their way, so that the ark would not fall into their hands ... Consequently one can say that the expression "the ark before them" is a figurative expression like the prophet's saying "The Lord is before me" ... "The Lord is at my right hand," or we say the Lord is before us in this matter or the Lord is in our midst, and in all these linguistic expressions the intent is to bring out God's leadership and the people's following.

10.17.3.en: Note: some interpreters see that only in the first journey, and as an exception, the ark did actually go before them as an encouragement to the people and to reassure them.

10.18.0.en: As for the pillar of cloud, which signifies God's leadership, it went before the people to guide, and shaded them in divine care from the burning sun of the desert.

10.19.1.en: These two verses mention a prayer of praise that Moses used to repeat when the ark was lifted onto the shoulders, saying as the ark was lifted: Rise up, O Lord, and let all the enemies of Your people, spiritual or human, flee and vanish from before Your divine glory, for there is no place for whoever hates Your holy name and there is no one who can stand before You or challenge Your people who carry Your ark and Your holy name.

10.19.2.en: And when the ark was set down and rested in its place in the Holy of Holies, he used to repeat another prayer, also of praise to God, in which he says: Return, O Lord, and dwell in the midst of Your people, and bless the ten thousands and thousands of Your people Israel ... The Church took these words and prays them in the Litany of the Assemblies. As the priest turns toward the east he says "Rise up, O Lord" and let all Your enemies be scattered, and then the priest turns toward the west, that is, toward the people, and completes his prayer saying, "As for Your people, may they be, by blessing, thousands of thousands and ten thousands of ten thousands."

10.19.3.en: The ark went before the people, and it signifies God's dwelling in the midst of His people ... Do you let God go before your steps ... your thoughts ... your feelings ... your decisions ... If only you would do this with a praying heart, then God will always be with you as a guide and a close friend.

10.19.4.en: The punishment of murmuring - the manna and the quails

11.0.0.en: Complaining evilly: that is, murmuring, and their murmuring was plain in their words or deeds.

11.0.1.en: The ears of the Lord: a rhetorical expression meaning that everything they complained of in a spirit of murmuring was before the Lord. We do not know here, and the cause of the murmuring is not mentioned ... perhaps it was because of exhaustion or some troubles from the hardship of life in the wilderness, but it meant that the people had forgotten all that God had done with them, and therefore this murmuring was evil, so the wrath of God came upon this people who denied all the good, and He allowed a fire to be kindled, regardless of its causes, and it burned the outer parts of the camp. We do not know the number of people it destroyed or the amount of the loss of animals or tents. We note that the murmuring began at the edge of the camp, that is, among those dwelling far from the tent of meeting, that is, nearness to the Church protects us from many sins.

11.1.0.en: The people understood and felt that what happened was a divine punishment that came upon them, and therefore they went to Moses crying out and asking his intercession with God that He might lift His wrath from them. And indeed Moses went before God and entreated Him, asking Him to remove the punishment, and God answered and quenched the fires.

11.2.0.en: So that what happened might become a memorial throughout the generations, Moses and the people called the name of this place "Taberah," which means burning, so that they might remember that murmuring angers the Giver of good things, and perhaps a person is punished for his murmuring with a punishment he cannot bear and cries out afterward for its removal from him.

11.2.1.en: Beloved, the life of true thanksgiving is what saves a person from falling into murmuring and spares him many punishments ... Thank your God every day for what He has done with you, and thank Him also for the evil He has kept from you.

11.3.0.en: The mixt multitude: they are the incomers (foreigners) among the people, and most of them were Egyptians who went out with them from Egypt.

11.3.1.en: The source of the murmuring this time was the Egyptian few who accompanied the people on their journey, but soon the rebellion and murmuring spread through all the people of Israel, and they declared their longing to eat various foods such as meat, fish and vegetables, like leeks, onions and garlic, and fruit such as melons, and in this they fell into a great fallacy, since they said "freely" although they were slaves forced into the service of Pharaoh ... This is what lust does to a person when it takes possession of him ... it makes him forget God entirely and all His kindnesses, and he no longer remembers anything but his need and what he lacks of fleshly desires.

11.4.0.en: The people expressed their murmuring by saying "our soul is dried away," that is, our bodies have grown weak and our freshness has gone, and we have become weary of the repeated eating of the manna, which we loathe and our eyes see nothing but it.

11.4.1.en: If you long one day for something, why do you not ask for it gently from your heavenly Father who gives to all and upbraids not!! ... But beware of murmuring against the divine graces poured out on you ... for there are many in the world who hope for the crumbs of bread left over from you. Beware of arrogance ... beware of murmuring ... lest God's grace be taken from you, for there is no gift without increase except that which is without thanksgiving, as St. Isaac the Syrian said.

11.5.0.en: Coriander seed: small grains whose color is between yellow and slightly green. Bdellium: a kind of yellow gum inclining to white, with a pleasant smell, used like incense, and in the form of flakes.

11.5.1.en: So that the divine inspiration may show us how wrong the people of the children of Israel were in their murmuring, it makes clear to us what the manna is: it is the free divine gift from God who loves His people, and its appearance was like small yellow grains resembling coriander seeds and flakes of bdellium.

11.6.0.en: Cakes: that is, bread baked on a flat stone, which is unleavened bread made on the hot stone in the desert (Gen 18:6). God sent it down at night with the dew, that is, before dawn, and the people did not sow it or toil for it, but all they did was gather it early, and they ground it and it became like flour and could be cooked or made into bread. Its taste was sweet, resembling the taste of cakes kneaded with oil, and its taste also like wafers made with honey (Ex 16:31), and the meaning is that because of the blessing of God the food was free and its taste was as though oil and honey had been put on it.

11.7.s.en: (4) Moses' complaint and God's reply to it

11.7.0.en: As the people's murmuring increased and the lust for food took possession of them, it reached the point of weeping like children at the doors of their tents, that is, openly, and the murmuring spread from one person to another until it included all. As for Moses the servant and shepherd, his soul was greatly wearied and embittered by the state of the people, for he felt with his spiritual sense that what the people were doing greatly angered God and wounded Him. And when the soul of Moses overflowed and his pains increased, he turned to the Lord, raising his complaint and reproaching Him, saying "Wherefore have You dealt ill with Your servant," which is an unbecoming expression, because God never does ill to any of His children, but He who searches the hearts understood well what Moses wanted to say, and Moses' expression meant that the weight of the responsibility of shepherding this murmuring people was beyond his endurance.

11.7.1.en: I have not found favour in thy sight: You have not relieved me of the responsibility of leading the people and have not given me anyone to help me.

11.8.0.en: Moses continues in his complaining prayer to God, going on in his groaning, expressing his weariness with his people, and he reproaches God, saying: why do You oblige me with the burden of the father and mother responsible for carrying their son to the Promised Land, when I did not give birth to this people.

11.9.0.en: They murmur and weep to me asking me for meat, so from where can I provide them meat enough for them? This people has become a heavy load that I cannot bear alone.

11.10.0.en: As the weariness of Moses the prophet increased, his soul became very distressed, so that he reached a degree of despair and depression in which he wished for death, and he expressed that by asking God "Kill me out of hand," and Moses regarded his death as a favor that God would do him, for by his death he would put an end to his misery and unbearable weariness.

11.10.1.en: We can draw some spiritual lessons from the position of Moses (vv. 10-15:)

11.10.2.en: 1- Moses was the meekest of men by the testimony of God, but the hardness of the people and their murmuring together with the greatness of the responsibility made him weak and shaken, and the lesson learned here is that every person is liable to human weakness, however great his holiness.

11.10.3.en: 2- Moses' recourse to God teaches us that there is no way to solve our psychological and spiritual problems except by prayer to God.

11.10.4.en: 3- Despite the weaknesses and unexpected words that Moses' prayer carried, we also learn that he spoke with God frankly and his prayer carried all his true inner feelings, and for this reason God answered his prayer at once, as we shall see.

11.10.5.en: Take refuge in God in all your problems, however hard, and trust in His love, for He is able to give you rest and guide you, so that you walk assured and successful by His strength.

11.11.0.en: The Lord did not reproach Moses and was not angry with him, for God knows perfectly the background of matters and appreciates what came from human weakness, especially since God Himself testified of Moses that he was meeker than all men (ch. 12:3), and this means that if any other person had been the leader of this people, he would not have endured, and his weariness and anger would have been many times more than Moses'.

11.11.1.en: But we find that God wanted to solve the problem for Moses positively by appointing helpers and counselors to help him in leading the people, so He asked him to choose seventy men and come to the tent of meeting. We note that God left the choice to Moses, but He also specified for him that these seventy be of the wise elders known to the people; and we note also that this tradition remained with the Jews after their settlement, so we know that the Sanhedrin council consisted of seventy men, and Christ also chose, with the twelve disciples, seventy apostles ...

11.12.0.en: I will come down: a human expression that God used to indicate that the events that will come are God's own will.

11.12.1.en: God continues His speech to Moses and says to him, when you gather with the seventy before the tent of meeting I will speak with you before them and I will give them of My Holy Spirit as I gave you, so that they too may be qualified to share with you in leading this heavy people.

11.12.2.en: If you are a servant or a person in charge, be careful to involve others with you, for distributing responsibilities lightens many burdens on you and raises up a generation of leaders after you, but you must choose the best, as the Lord commanded Moses.

11.13.s.en: (5) The promise of meat and the coming of the Spirit of God upon the elders

11.13.0.en: God commanded Moses to command the people to sanctify themselves, and the sanctification was spiritual by repentance and bodily by washing their clothes and their bodies, and this sanctification always preceded standing before the Lord or receiving something great from Him.

11.13.1.en: The event that followed the sanctification was that God would give them meat to eat, for He had heard their murmuring, "ye have wept in the ears of the Lord," and their belief that slavery in Egypt had been better for them, and therefore God will give them what they asked, which is the eating of meat.

11.14.0.en: The eating of meat will be not for one day or several days but for a whole month, and they will eat of it greedily until it comes out at their nostrils, that is, its smell comes out of their noses as a result of the filling of the belly with this meat, and after that they will loathe it and abhor it from their eating too much of it, because of their rejection of the manna and their murmuring against God and their lust for eating meat.

11.15.0.en: Moses wondered at God's words, which seemed strange to him and hard to carry out, and he also expressed his astonishment in a manner that seems to us unexpected from Moses ... for he addressed God, saying: from where? and how? The number of footmen counted for war is six hundred thousand, apart from the rest of the people, so the total number of the people is more than two million. Would all the fish of the sea and all the sheep and cattle available suffice for them, and how can that be for a whole month?!!

11.16.0.en: God bore Moses' human weakness and the weariness of his soul, but He also rebuked him, that perhaps he might awake and examine himself: had he forgotten all that the Lord had done before in Egypt and during the crossing and at the receiving of the tables of the Law?! So He asks him "Is the Lord's hand waxed short?" that is, is there anything I am not able to do ... is My power unable to do anything?! But you will see soon My great power, and then you will realize whether My promises come to pass or not ...!

11.16.1.en: How long is Your patience, my God, with Your children ... What Moses said is unreasonable, and yet You humble Yourself and condescend to speak with him and converse with him and reproach him and rebuke him, but with patience and love. So You do with us also in many cases ... Forgive us, my God, our ignorance and continue Your mercies upon us.

11.17.0.en: The first scene ended, which was the speech and complaint of Moses to the Lord, and here we are before a new scene from which we understand that Moses had indeed chosen the seventy elders and they gathered around the Tent. When they gathered, the glory of the Lord was manifested in the form of a pillar of cloud and He began His speech with Moses, and the Lord God gave the seventy elders holy gifts, and as a sign of the coming of the Spirit of God upon them they prophesied. Prophesying here means that they uttered words and things they had had no knowledge of before, whether future matters or teachings and preaching to the people that they had not been able to do before.

11.17.1.en: But they did no more: that is, other gifts were not given to them, like the miracles that Moses performed, but the gift was limited to showing God's choice of them, so they only prophesied.

11.18.0.en: Two elders called "Eldad and Medad" of the seventy stayed behind and did not come before the Tent with the rest of the elders. We do not know the reason for their not coming, but perhaps it was their feeling of unworthiness. Despite their not coming and their remaining in the camp among the people, the Spirit of the Lord came upon them, and the sign of that was that they prophesied like the rest of the seventy.

11.19.0.en: Their news spread, and a young man came informing Moses that they were prophesying in the camp like the rest of the seventy. When "Joshua the son of Nun," Moses' first servant and closest disciple, heard, he was seized by jealousy for the honor of Moses, and felt that what happened with "Eldad and Medad" should not have happened to them, as they were the ones who stayed behind from God's and Moses' calling to them; so Joshua asked Moses whether he should go to them to prevent them, even by force, from prophesying.

11.20.0.en: The heart of Moses was different, and he reproached his disciple Joshua, "Are you jealous for my honor because these two elders did not listen to my word?! ... I (Moses) wished that the Spirit of the Lord would come upon all the people and they would all become prophets. This position shows us the breadth of the heart of Moses, which was distinguished from the narrower heart of his disciple, for the truly spiritual man rejoices in the filling of the Church of God with gifts and does not oppose them with a war of mistaken jealousy.

11.21.s.en: (6) The sending of the quails and the punishment of murmuring and lust

11.21.0.en: After the end of God's speech with Moses, he and the elders returned to the camp, and afterward a strong wind blew from the south, that is, from the direction of the Red Sea, and this wind brought huge numbers of the "quail" bird and cast them upon the people sitting in the camp ... To know the size of the flocks of these birds that God sent to His people, the inspired text used the expression "as it were a day's journey on this side, and as it were a day's journey on the other side," and a day's journey is about 35 kilometers, because a person walks about 5 km an hour and walks about 7 hours a day, so a day's journey = 5 × 7 = 35 km, that is, an area 35 km in breadth around the camp on all sides, and this area is very large, so it contained flocks of quail enough and overflowing, far more than the need of the people.

11.21.1.en: It was also of God's care that He made the height of these flocks no more than one meter above the surface of the ground, "two cubits," so that the people could catch them and hunt them ... Most likely the quail bird is the migratory quail, which does indeed pass over the desert of Sinai.

11.22.0.en: The people sinned greatly, for although God promised the people that meat would not fail for a month and that there would be more than enough for their need ... the people, driven by their lust and their lack of reliance on God's promises, continued all day and night and until the morning of the second day in hunting and gathering the quail with an eagerness and lust that were greatly exaggerated ... so that even the one who gathered least gathered of the birds what equals the load of ten donkeys, so they did not take only enough but took more for storing, and they "spread them out," that is, salted them and spread them around the camp.

11.22.1.en: Ten homers: the homer is a measure estimated at about 230 liters, and they used to estimate the homer by a donkey's load, that is, what a single donkey can carry.

11.23.0.en: Greed, gluttony, unbelief of God's words and haste to store in large quantities were behind God's great wrath against His people, for instead of praying and thanking God for what He had done for them, they opened their greedy mouths to eat and fill their bellies.

11.23.1.en: God's stroke came strong, for before they finished their eating, that is, while the remains of the meat were still between their teeth, God punished them with a very great stroke, which most interpreters see as a painful plague of which many of the people became victims ... And since the people knew that this punishment was just and knew that its cause was the evil lust that had taken possession of them and made them murmur against God, they called the place where they buried their victims "Kibroth-hattaavah," that is, the graves of lust.

11.23.2.en: How evil is the sin of lust and what it brings upon a person, for it brought down David and destroyed the strength of Samson, and how great also was God's punishment of them ... Beware, beloved, of the lust of the flesh, which has humbled many.

11.24.0.en: And from the place of burial of the victims of the lust of the flesh the cloud was lifted again, as a divine sign that it was necessary to journey again, and the pillar stood in a place called Hazeroth north of Mount Sinai, so the people encamped there and pitched their tents.
